Check the app in a different language if offered.

o: Test levels: single parts, parts together, whole app, real users.
Note whether the fault occurs offline, on Wi-Fi or on mobile data.
Picture or recording; how often it happens.

questions.q: In "Run on devices Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: One idea per case.
Testing shows bugs exist; it cannot show none exist.
Use at least two device sizes and two system versions.
Check the privacy text matches what the app really collects.

questions.q: In "Bug reports Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Types: function, usability, speed, safety, access, compatibility.
Check basic safety: sign-out, data shown on screen, permissions asked.
Test rotating the screen in the middle of a task.
Use a clean test account for each run.

questions.q: In "Speed, safety and access Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Retest fixes and a few related areas.
Read the store description and any help page, then list five promises the app makes; each promise is a test you can write straight away.
Check speed by timing the launch from tap to first usable screen on a mid-range phone; under 3 seconds is a good target, and note anything over 5 seconds.
After the fix, retest the exact steps from the original report and also run three nearby cases, since a fix in one place can quietly break another.

questions.q: In "Analyse and prioritise Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?

Find patterns: one cause may explain five bugs.
Steps to reproduce, expected, actual, device and version.
Read the store description and any help page, then list five promises the app makes; each promise is a test you can write straight away.
